scope: Unchanged unrelated-host dry/wet transfer of the official Poly Haven Rough Concrete 2K PNG source
accepted: The source remains a five-map, hash-bound, decoded, provider-file package with provider MD5 and Videoer SHA-256 evidence.
A texture appearance may inherit live water/history/construction responses only when every modeled-unit target declares the same response; incomplete or ambiguous inheritance fails closed.
Repeated surface binding now replaces stale target metadata instead of accumulating contradictory declarations.
Derived scenes rebase every geometry, motion, rig, fixture, water/history, overlay and finish dependency relative to the new scene and record source/replacement hashes.
Dry and wet intended-camera probes were rendered with canonical Blender 4.5.13 and the benchmark was not modified.
rejected: Dry concrete remains bleached, chalky and too uniform across the regular paving units.
Wet response forms broad glassy contiguous regions with abrupt patch boundaries instead of convincing fine drainage and material absorption variation.
Disabled uncalibrated displacement correctly prevents invented relief but leaves no reviewed silhouette-scale surface breakup.
The facade, glazing and interior host remain clean sparse blockouts, so the assembled scene is not photographic even if a future paving source improves.
learning: A legally and technically sound source package is necessary but does not establish useful production material character.
Appearance replacement and causal construction response are separate contracts and must be composed explicitly.
Wet/dry transfer is a stronger audit than a neutral swatch because it exposes response erasure, scene-path portability and water-boundary defects before publication.
nextGenericChange: Acquire and compare a stronger homogeneous concrete source using the unchanged provider and transfer contracts, then improve renderer-independent multi-scale surface history and water boundary/coverage behavior. Do not tune or rerender the cinematic benchmark for this work.
productionClothing: Queued behind the active reusable environment/material work: garment panels and pattern construction, seams, hems, thickness, shoulder and armhole quality, base weights and correctives, folds and wrinkles, cloth materials, selective simulation, and temporal verification. This is reusable-system work, not benchmark-specific polishing.
